messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm prepping a roles schema migration (roles.v3) that changes how default roles are derived and adds a TTL on audit_entry.role_snapshot. Need a canary plan + KMS key access check before running on prod. @jon @elena are you around?
jon: around. can you paste the SQL and the exact shards you want to target? :eyes:
maria: SQL preview below — it's idempotent but touches the default role seed and bumps the audit snapshots to keep last 90 days only. plan is canary on auth-shard-5 then roll by shard.
```sql
BEGIN;
-- ensure seed exists
INSERT INTO roles (id, name, is_default, created_at)
SELECT '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001', 'default', true, now()
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM roles WHERE name = 'default');

-- flip legacy default flag for users relying on legacy mapping
UPDATE user_roles ur
SET role_id = r.id
FROM roles r
WHERE ur.role_name = 'default' AND r.name = 'default' AND ur.role_id IS NULL;

-- add TTL marker for role snapshot in audit entries
ALTER TABLE audit_entry ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS role_snapshot_valid_until timestamptz;
UPDATE audit_entry SET role_snapshot_valid_until = now() + interval '90 days' WHERE role_snapshot IS NOT NULL;
COMMIT;
```
elena: small question — is the role_snapshot encrypted? we rely on KMS on prod for role snapshots in private deployments. sec-bot: KMS rotation notice — key projects/redwood-key (v3) rotated 2026-02-12 02:01 UTC. verify access before migration.
kevin: on KMS — make sure the migration process doesn't write new snapshots with a different key id. If the column is unencrypted at first, we need a plan to re-encrypt older snapshots using current key.
maria: current plan: we won't re-encrypt in migration. migration only sets TTL and ensures seed exists. re-encrypt will be a follow-up job. but need to confirm the migration doesn't read/decrypt anything that would fail with rotated keys.
jon: good. canary checklist: 1) dry-run on auth-shard-5 2) verify audit_ingest_lag < 30s 3) run smoke tests for role binding 4) ensure no 5xx or authz denials spike 5) check KMS decryption errors in logs.
sam: add to checklist: verify `service_account` fallthroughs. we found a previous issue where missing default role allowed escalation for federated service accounts.
maria: yes — thanks. mitigating guard: auth-service will short-circuit and default to a transient deny if user->role mapping returns null for 2+ requests in a minute. I can push a patch canary to auth-service at the same time.
kevin: any rollback playbook? if we see explosions, what are quick steps?
maria: rollback plan (summary):
- stop migration runner
- revert auth-service patch (hotfix rollback)
- run recovery SQL to reseed default role id from backup: `INSERT INTO roles (id, name, is_default) VALUES ('00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001','default',true) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;`
- run audit repair: `UPDATE audit_entry SET role_snapshot = (select role_snapshot from audit_entry_bak where audit_entry.id = audit_entry_bak.id) WHERE role_snapshot IS NULL;`
- open incident channel and run postmortem.
elena: we should also add a DB constraint to prevent user_roles.role_id from being NULL in prod, but that needs a migration window. for now add a monitoring alert on `user_roles_null_rate` >= 0.1%
jon: thumbs-up. when do you want to run the canary?
maria: aiming for 2026-03-21 03:00 UTC (off-peak). will run auth-shard-5 only, then wait 30m, check the checklist. if all green, we roll next shard every hour.
kevin: make sure CI/QA runs the new auth integration tests that assert deny-on-null semantics. I'll add them now.
sam: also add a post-canary smoke prompt set for product owners — they can run known-user checks (login, role-based feature gates)
maria: noted. @sec-bot can you run a quick KMS access verification for the deploy user and post results?
sec-bot: KMS access check for deployer@redwood: OK for projects/redwood-key:v3. No IAM denials in the last 7 days.
jon: LGTM. I can be on watch during the canary window.
elena: I'll be nearby for KMS logs and will tail auth-service for decryption errors.
maria: great — final note: if we see any sudden increase in `authz_failures` or `user_roles_null_rate`, abort and open incident. I'll annotate the runbook and post the canary command in #eng-oncall before start. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
